S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent, excessive worry and apprehensive expectation about multiple domains of life (e.g., work, finances, health, relationships) occurring more days than not for at least six months, and difficult for the person to control. The anxiety is typically accompanied by physical and cognitive manifestations such as restlessness, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance, leading to clinically significant distress or functional impairment. Onset is often gradual and can follow chronic stressors; the course tends to be chronic with waxing and waning severity, frequently co-occurring with depressive and other anxiety disorders. It is distinguished from normal worry by its pervasiveness, intensity, uncontrollability, and impairment, and from other anxiety disorders by the broad, non–situation-specific nature of the worry rather than being tied to discrete phobic stimuli, panic attacks, or obsessions.

patient.personality: She is an empathetic, creatively driven young woman who juggles structured ambition with artistic side projects and a tendency to overcommit herself.
patient.stressor: The onset of her difficulties traces back to a turbulent separation from her high school partner about a year and a half ago, which coincided with her moving out of a shared apartment and taking on full responsibility for her own bills while working in a high-pressure customer service role. Already someone who took others’ emotions to heart, she began second-guessing every decision—from whether she had chosen the right career path to whether she could realistically pursue a communications degree and UX writing certification while keeping up with rent and expectations at work. Over the following year, she increasingly filled her free time with new creative projects and volunteering to distract herself, but found that the more she tried to plan and control her future, the more mentally preoccupied she became with potential missteps in her relationships, finances, and career, leading to missed social plans and declining performance at work. She finally sought psychiatric help after her supervisor noted her growing errors and she realized that her constant mental preoccupation with “what if” scenarios about her relationships, job stability, and academic plans was making it hard to function day to day.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I’m constantly worrying about everything all at once, and I can’t seem to shut my mind off no matter what I do.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I just lie there staring at the ceiling for hours, my brain running through work calls I might mess up or how I’ll pay rent if my hours get cut, and even when I finally pass out I wake up at like 4 or 5 in the morning with my heart racing and can’t shut it off enough to go back to sleep, so I drag myself through the day feeling like I never actually rested.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: I feel wiped out pretty much all the time now, like even after a full night in bed my body is heavy and my head feels foggy, so just getting through an eight-hour shift on the phones and then trying to work on my portfolio or class applications at night feels like I’m pushing through wet cement.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: My mind is constantly jumping from worrying that a slightly annoyed customer means my supervisor’s going to fire me, to thinking I’ll never save enough for school, to replaying my last relationship and convincing myself I’m going to mess up every future one too, like there’s this never-ending list of disasters I’m supposed to prevent.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: Even when I tell myself to stop, or put on music or try to draw or scroll TikTok, the 'what ifs' just barge back in—what if my card declines at the grocery store, what if I fail at UX and have to move back in with my parents, what if everyone’s secretly mad at me—and it snowballs until I feel like I’ve lost control of my own thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
S059.manifestation: At work, I’ll be in the middle of a call or logging a ticket and suddenly my brain just blanks out or veers off into some anxiety spiral about my future, and I’ll catch myself rereading the same line three times or asking a customer to repeat basic info because I literally cannot hold it in my head.
